questions.topic: Developmental and Health: How a Self-View Is Built
questions.stem: In a revision exercise, A child's self-view shifts after peer feedback and social comparison; what builds self-concept here?

options.misconception: confuses Genetics alone with the supported claim Feedback and comparison.
confuses body with self
reads the evidence as Random mood instead of Feedback and comparison.

questions.explanation: Self-concept builds from feedback, comparison, and experience. Genetics and growth alone do not account for the shift.

questions.topic: Developmental and Health: What Makes a Stage a Stage
questions.stem: Faced with this description, A child grows taller but shows no new reasoning; explain why this is not a stage shift?

answer.exemplar: Growth in size is quantitative, whereas a stage shift requires qualitative reorganization of thought, so height alone does not mark a new stage.

questions.explanation: Stages require qualitative change in reasoning. Physical growth is quantitative and does not create a stage shift.

questions.topic: Developmental and Health: What a Maturation Explanation Claims

stimulus.body: A baby sits up at six months without training, while a trained baby of the same age does not sit earlier. The milestone appears on a typical timetable regardless of practice.

questions.stem: A source note on developmental and Health: What a Maturation Explanation Claims reads: "Maturation drives the milestone" Using that evidence, while going over a worked case, what does this pattern suggest?

options.misconception: requires a model
contradicted by data
requires reinforcement

questions.explanation: The milestone appears on a typical timetable regardless of training, indicating maturation. Training, imitation, and conditioning were not decisive.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Developmental and Health: Critical and Sensitive Periods
questions.stem: On a timed practice set, A skill not learned in a narrow window is permanently lost, while a skill learned later is merely accented. What two-stage period distinction is shown?

options.text: A critical period brings permanent loss while a sensitive period leaves only an accent
Early care builds expectations that are carried into new relationships
options.misconception: assumes expectations form only in later relationships, not from early care

options.text: Gradual vocabulary growth is followed by sudden reorganization into grammar
options.misconception: believes development is entirely continuous with no qualitative jump

options.text: Goodness of fit between temperament and setting determines adjustment
options.misconception: treats temperament as uniformly good or bad regardless of environment

questions.explanation: Stage one is a critical period with permanent loss; stage two is a sensitive period with accent only. The distinction is rigidity versus flexibility.
